messages.author: 89c04f2e40dabf01
messages.subject: Learning about shiny
parts:
I am just starting to explore shiny and have a few questions about its functionality before I dive too deeply into learning to use it. My current goal is to build a GUI (web-based app is nice) that makes it easier for users to implement my functions.

For example, suppose I want to allow a user to read in a datafile (say .csv) and then use the lm() function to run a regression all from a web-based app with point and click options to choose the files, as well as the variables to be used in the regression.

I cannot tell from the tutorials if this is a good use of shiny or if it has another intended purpose.

Thank you for your advice. 

Harold

messages.author: 33dc9c6d026ee296
messages.subject: Re: Learning about shiny
parts:
That sounds to me like a realtively simple and appropriate application of Shiny -- a good place to start for your first app.  You might want to decide first, though, how you are going to deploy your app:  on a Shiny server, or thourhg shinyapps.io?

Homer

messages.author: e1656d208b1207ce
messages.subject: Re: Learning about shiny
parts:
I would second that this is exactly the type of app shiny is designed for. You can check out my project shinyData, which supports reading csv files, manipulating the dataframe and visualizing the data with the powerful ggplot2 package. My app is probably too complicated for you to start as your first shiny app, but can show you what shiny is capable of and maybe give you useful hints on how to go about this.

Yindeng
